title: Confession and Beauty before God
english: by the incomparable superiority of creative power

Do not command them to depart into the deep abyss, having sent away a voice of pity; O God, do not torment us before the time (Ps 95:6). He who has acquired beauty through the loveliness of virtue, and presents this innate [beauty] with thanksgiving and confession before God, according to the one saying, 'The Lord of powers, I stood before Him' (Ps 95:6), [is such]; for everyone sinning flees from standing before God. For the lawless do not remain before His eyes.

Indeed, even Adam, after sinning with the woman, flees from the face of the Lord God, being ashamed, but rather fearing to be seen by Him. In this way also the Tempter goes out from the face of the Lord God, not that it is possible to flee from God and be far from His face, but because the wicked, deceiving themselves with false glory, thought they could hide from God, upon whom they act impiously; for even if they should succeed in hiding from God, it is not that they are [actually hidden], but rather they possess such a disposition that, if it were possible, they would have wanted to be far from God, being ashamed of the rays of His eyes.

But the diligent, through much boldness and the freedom of the gaze before God, have stood as genuine servants of justice, saying, 'Look upon me and have mercy on me' (Ps 51:1), and 'The eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous and His gaze upon their prayer' (Ps 34:15). Do not be troubled, since we, the ones confessing and possessing beauty before the Lord, participate in [this]; and often, according to the Scripture, regarding those having certain [states], it is said through the analogies of those states; for the Apostle, writing to men, says concerning him and them, 'That we might become the righteousness of God' (2 Cor 5:21) (meaning clearly, in Him, Christ).
